observations: Black DSLR camera body with 'Nikon' logo on the prism in photo 0 and 1.
Model 'D7100' is printed on the front of the camera body in photo 0 and 1.
The camera is positioned in front of a box clearly marked 'Nikon' and 'D7100' in photo 0 and 1.
The lens mount is open in photo 1, showing the internal mirror.
No lens, batteries, or silicone case are visible in either photo.
Watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI MONSY LUV' appears on both photos.

claims.evidence: There is no video of the camera operating or sample images provided.
No batteries are shown in the photos.
No case is shown in the photos.
Photos 0 and 1 clearly show Nikon branding on the camera and the box.

risks.risk: High shutter count or mechanical failure
risks.proof: A screenshot of the shutter count from a recent photo's EXIF data.
A clear, high-resolution photo of the sensor/mirror assembly.
A photo showing the camera alongside the 2 batteries and the silicone case.

proof_requests: Photo of the camera's LCD screen showing the model and serial number.
Photo of the two batteries and the silicone case mentioned in the text.
A video showing the camera powering on and taking a photo.
A recent photo file to check the shutter count via EXIF data.
response.reason: The seller's text explicitly identifies the brand as Canon, but the photos clearly show a Nikon D7100 camera and box. This fundamental contradiction between the description and the visual evidence is a common indicator of a scam.
